top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a single mechanism, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime with the light shift cancelled by design, that is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion control prizes. It has been reproduced independently at about 1e-18 by JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST, and has already produced measured physics (centimetre-scale gravitational redshift, many-body clock effects, bounds on drifting constants). The two-name credit cleanly separates proposal (Katori) from record realisation (Ye), unlike the topological-insulator alternative where the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap cannot be repaired. IceCube (P002) is a real discovery but its confirmation so far lies within IceCube channels and the three-name cut is a judgement call, so it ranks second; a deserving prize still beats no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no known tie to Katori, Ye or the IceCube names, and clocks and astroparticle physics are far from my work on electronic-structure theory and magnetism
